title: SIU probing death of man Tasered by Peel police
article: Guns drawn, Tasers out and loud yelling and screaming.

This is how neighbours describe what was a frantic scene Tuesday night between Peel Regional Police and a man in a house on Morningstar Dr., near Goreway Dr. and Derry Rd. E. in Malton, close to Pearson International Airport.
By the time media arrived on the scene, a 34-year-old man was "vital signs absent" and later died at hospital.
The remnants of emergency services equipment and life-saving medical apparatus were strewn over the driveway, which was protected by yellow police tape.
"I saw him being Tased," said a neighbour who gave the name Ack. "The police Tased him right at his front door and after it happened, all you could hear is screaming and crying."
Ack said the man was his long-time friend Matthew DiGiovanni.

"I talked to him today," Ack said Tuesday night at the scene. "He was OK but had a tough day in family court where he lost and was told he had to pay court costs in a battle over custody of his child."
Peel police tweeted that they had responded to a "disturbance" at 9:01 p.m. where they had an "interaction with a person."
But neighbours say they saw guns and a Taser drawn.

Since a person died during this call, the province's Special Investigation Unit has evoked its mandate. The SIU said police responded to a "domestic call." Two subject officers and one witness officer have been designated, the police watchdog said.
Neither the SIU or police have confirmed the identity of the deceased but his friend and several other neighbours confirmed it was DiGiovanni.
"His father, Joe, just recently died and he has been upset about that," a neighbour said.
The man has not been working but Ack said he had worked as a contractor in the past.
"He was a good kid," said Ack. "This is very sad."
The SIU is now in charge of the investigation to determine not only how all of this shook out, but if it was handled "appropriately" by police.
No one was suggesting anything untoward.
"He was a big guy," Ack said of why police may have needed to use a Taser.
He also suggested alcohol and narcotics may have also been involved.
